euronews.title: Estonia-Russia border closure sends residents rushing to cross before deadline
euronews.description: Families and travellers are queuing to cross from Russia into Estonia before all five road border crossings are shut on 1 December. The decision follows an alleged Russian-backed sabotage attempt, but has also raised concerns among people with relatives on both sides of the border.

euronews.title: Former Costa Concordia cruise ship captain released from prison on probation after nine years
euronews.description: The case dates back to January 2012, when the Costa Concordia ship struck rocks off the coast of Isola del Giglio in the Tyrrhenian Sea. The disaster claimed 32 lives.

euronews.description: The strike mainly targeted civilian infrastructure, Zelenskyy wrote on X. The attack comes after Russia vowed a 'painful' response to Ukraine's strike on the Crimean bridge.

euronews.title: EU budget: Costa pitches more cuts, Big Tech tax to break deadlock
euronews.description: European Council President António Costa proposes cutting the EU's 2028-2034 budget by nearly €200bn, a 10% reduction, to win over frugal countries. Cohesion funding is cut for the first time. A 3% digital services levy replaces a controversial corporate tax, and debt repayment is slowed down.

euronews.title: Strait of Hormuz: Athlete swims through war zone to expose war's environmental toll
euronews.description: British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh completed a 15-kilometre swim through the Strait of Hormuz over three days in November 2026, braving explosions and burning tankers nearby. His three-day challenge aimed to expose the environmental damage caused by the war with Iran.

euronews.title: European Union and Indonesia sign free trade deal after decade of talks
euronews.description: Trade between the EU and Indonesia was valued at €28.9 billion in 2025, with EU exports worth €10.2 billion and EU imports worth €18.7 billion.

euronews.description: A pilotless electric flying taxi has carried a passenger during a demonstration, on Friday 20 November 2026, in Japan's Yamanashi Prefecture. The Chinese-built aircraft took off vertically and flew autonomously, offering a glimpse of a possible future for urban transport.

euronews.title: Anthropic worker claims to have solved famed 167-year-old maths problem with help of AI
euronews.description: Brian Greene, a professor of physics and mathematics at Columbia University in New York, called Alpöge's proof potentially "one of the greatest mathematical breakthroughs in the past two centuries."

euronews.title: Off the Record: Europe shrugs as Trump's Yalta knockoff flops
euronews.description: In this week’s newsletter, Euronews Political Correspondent Jorge Liboreiro unpacks the fallout from the much-hyped “Yalta 2.0”, describing the outcome as a political nothingburger.

euronews.title: Pentagon declassifies new UFO footage filmed by US military
euronews.description: The US Department of War has published its eighth release of declassified historical files on unidentified anomalous phenomena, with further documents expected to be made public.

euronews.title: Fossil fuel row sees COP31 talks spill into overtime
euronews.description: A number of countries, including France and Panama, released a letter on Friday insisting that a deal include "a clear transition away from fossil fuels."

rfi.title: French court finds racism played role in police beating of black music producer
rfi.description: A French court has handed down prison sentences to three police officers for the violent assault of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020, ruling that racism was an aggravating factor in a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police brutality and racial discrimination.

rfi.title: National Assembly backs greater legal protection for police using firearms
rfi.description: France's parliament has approved legislation giving police officers greater legal protection when using their firearms, prompting fierce criticism from rights groups who warn it could make it harder to investigate alleged police brutality. The government insists the measure is needed to protect officers carrying out increasingly demanding duties.

rfi.title: France must change or 'risk losing' overseas territories, former PM tells RFI
rfi.description: France's territories outside Europe are a major strategic asset, giving it a foothold on five continents and in three oceans. Yet Paris has long been accused of neglecting the nearly 3 million people living outside mainland France, who face deep economic and social inequalities. With calls for independence growing, former prime minister Manuel Valls warns that France risks losing its overseas territories unless it radically changes its relationship with them.

rfi.title: Former PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid with warning to far right
rfi.description: Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin has announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election, promising to restore France's international influence, tackle growing inequality and challenge the rise of the far right. The veteran conservative also delivered a blistering assessment of President Emmanuel Macron's leadership, accusing him of allowing the country's political and social divisions to deepen.

rfi.title: Cost of living protests set to continue across Europe over weekend
rfi.description: Protests across Europe against conditions in schools, housing and the soaring cost of living are set to continue throughout the weekend, with hundreds of thousands expected to take to the streets in countries across the continent – including France, Belgium, Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom.

rfi.title: UN climate talks run into overtime as countries clash over fossil fuel cuts
rfi.description: Deep divisions over fossil fuels and financial support for poorer nations pushed the Cop31 climate summit in Turkey beyond its scheduled closing day on Friday, as nearly 200 countries struggled to agree on how to tackle global warming.

rfi.title: Turkey seizes control of last major independent news channel amid fraud scandal
rfi.description: Turkey's last operating independent TV news channel has fallen under state control, as President Recep Tayyip Erdogan scrambles to contain a wave of public fury over a $20 billion investment fund scandal that has swallowed the life savings of hundreds of thousands of people in the country.

rfi.title: French Greens candidate gives hard-left Mélenchon a boost in presidential race
rfi.description: French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has said an alliance with the Greens "should be possible", after the head of the Greens tentatively agreed to back him, angering moderates on the centre-left.

rfi.title: France probes suspected leaks from interior ministry to far-right National Rally
rfi.description: France has opened a probe into suspicions that a senior official at the interior ministry leaked secret information to the far-right National Rally (RN) party, which is itself facing a number of investigations, prosecutors have said.

rfi.title: Depardieu and Houellebecq accused of gang rape on French film set
rfi.description: Paris prosecutors have opened an investigation after an actress filed a complaint alleging that she was raped by a group including actor Gérard Depardieu and high-profile French author Michel Houellebecq on the set of the film Thalasso in 2018.

rfi.title: EU and UK agree 'landmark' deal at Burnham's Brussels summit
rfi.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU's top officials on Friday sealed deals to ease trade and youth mobility at a summit in Brussels, billed as a first step in a push to rebuild ties after Brexit.

rfi.title: Nigeria moves to end prison sentences for attempted suicide
rfi.description: President Bola Tinubu has asked the Nigerian parliament to decriminalise attempted ​suicide and provide support for people who have tried to take their own lives. The move is aimed at ​treating ‌suicide attempts as a ⁠mental health issue rather than a criminal offence, in a country where access to psychological healthcare is limited and suicidal thoughts are often treated as a spiritual affliction.

rfi.title: Africa accounts for half of world's children living in conflict zones, NGO warns
rfi.description: Around 260 million children in Africa were living close to armed conflict in 2025 – amounting to two in five, a larger proportion than ever previously recorded, the charity Save the Children said in a report on Thursday. Worldwide, nearly one in four children lived near fighting.

rfi.title: Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya, says top UN court
rfi.description: Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, the International Court of Justice said on Thursday in an historic ruling, ordering refugees be given safe passage home and awarded compensation.

rfi.title: EU delays new methane emissions rules until 2029 despite climate concerns
rfi.description: The European Union has agreed to postpone new methane emissions regulations for two years, giving the oil and gas industry more time to adapt amid mounting pressure on global energy markets. But environmental groups warn the decision risks undermining climate ambitions.

rfi.title: Europe left out in the cold as Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China
rfi.description: As the leaders of the United States, China and Russia held historic talks in the Chinese city of Shenzhen on Thursday, representatives of the European Union – the world's largest trading bloc – were conspicuously absent, despite the fact the discussions could have far-reaching consequences for Europe.

rfi.title: France raises bird flu alert to highest level as infections spread across Europe
rfi.description: France is raising its avian flu alert to the highest level from Friday, bringing new restrictions on poultry movements as authorities seek to contain the spread of the virus. The decision comes amid a rise in infections among wild birds across Europe, particularly along migration routes crossing France.

rfi.title: Podcast: Living on the breadline, France's 35-hour week and a divisive tax
rfi.description: The French government's decision to raise the minimum wage has failed to satisfy protesters struggling to make ends meet amid the cost-of-living crisis. Also, did the introduction of the 35-hour working week actually help reduce unemployment? The evidence is mixed. And a look at the history of France's second-largest tax, the CSG, and why it's dividing politicians.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : à cinq mois de l’élection, l’inquiétude grandit au sein du camp présidentiel, toujours incapable de s’unir
lemonde.description: Le débat autour d’une primaire à droite et au centre met en lumière la difficulté d’une stratégie claire au sein de l’ancienne majorité, prise entre des considérations individuelles et des fractures idéologiques.

lemonde.title: « On est devenus “street medics” parce qu’on se sentait impuissants face aux violences » : à la rencontre des bénévoles qui secourent les manifestants blessés
lemonde.description: Depuis le début du mouvement social, les « secouristes de rue » sont au cœur des cortèges. Contamination au gaz lacrymogène, plaies, crises d’angoisse… ils prodiguent les premiers gestes aux manifestants, sur fond de recours croissant aux armes par les forces de l’ordre – y compris contre eux.

lemonde.title: Au Brésil, une nouvelle génération de gauche s’apprête à faire son entrée au Parlement
lemonde.description: Lors des législatives du 4 octobre, les électeurs ont voté pour de jeunes députés progressistes. Alors que le gouvernement de Lula propose des économies budgétaires, ces élus veulent veiller à ce qu’il respecte ses promesses de campagne.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : la Finlande soupçonne un hélicoptère russe d’être entré dans son espace aérien, quelques heures après une attaque au drone d’un cargo russe en mer Baltique
lemonde.description: « Cette violation présumée de l’espace aérien pourrait être liée à des opérations de sauvetage ou de surveillance menées à la suite des dommages subis par un navire cargo dans le golfe de Finlande », a déclaré le ministre de la défense finlandais, Antti Häkkänen.

lemonde.title: A Genève, la communauté internationale échoue à interdire les robots tueurs
lemonde.description: Alors que la menace des systèmes d’armes létales autonomes, désormais assistées par l’intelligence artificielle, se fait chaque jour plus précise dans les zones de combat, la Russie, les Etats-Unis et Israël se sont opposés à l’ouverture de négociations pour un traité international sur ce type d’armes.

lemonde.title: A Agen, les irréductibles opposants à la ligne à grande vitesse Bordeaux-Toulouse : « On a un pays qui est superbe et ils vont venir le massacrer. Qu’est-ce qu’on va laisser à nos enfants ? »
lemonde.description: Dans le Lot-et-Garonne, les déboisements préalables au chantier de la ligne à grande vitesse Bordeaux-Toulouse sont sur le point de commencer. Autour d’Agen, les opposants à ce projet, lancé en 2009, balaient les arguments d’attractivité économique et de gain de temps pour dénoncer son coût exorbitant et son impact désastreux sur l’environnement.

lemonde.title: Dans la défense, le rapprochement entre le Canada et l’Union européenne prend corps
lemonde.description: Sur fond de tensions géopolitiques mondiales et d’incertitudes quant à l’engagement américain, Ottawa et Bruxelles coopèrent sur le soutien à l’Ukraine et le réarmement du Vieux Continent.

lemonde.title: Florian Sitbon, adjoint à la culture au maire de Paris, veut « mettre l’artiste au cœur de la ville »
lemonde.description: L’ancien metteur en scène, nommé en mars auprès d’Emmanuel Grégoire, prévoit la mise en place d’un guichet pour aider artistes et programmateurs qui voient leur liberté de création mise à mal.

lemonde.title: Génocide des Rohingya : la Cour internationale de justice rend un arrêt pour l’histoire
lemonde.description: La plus haute Cour de l’ONU établit pour la première fois la responsabilité d’un Etat, la Birmanie, dans « le crime des crimes ». Alors que l’Afrique du Sud a saisi l’institution contre Israël, accusant l’Etat hébreu d’un génocide contre les Palestiniens de Gaza, l’arrêt prononcé jeudi pourrait faire jurisprudence.

lemonde.title: Quand Elon Musk alertait sur les dangers de l’IA
lemonde.description: L’entrepreneur de la tech, qui fait l’objet d’un documentaire à charge actuellement en salle aux Etats-Unis, vante aujourd’hui les mérites de l’intelligence artificielle. En 2017 pourtant, il partageait ses craintes en s’appuyant sur le film « Le Cerveau d’acier », dont il est fan.

lemonde.title: France-Argentine : face aux Pumas, le XV de France veut confirmer l’« exploit » réalisé contre les Springboks
lemonde.description: Antoine Dupont et ses coéquipiers affrontent les joueurs argentins, samedi, au Stade de France, lors de la dernière journée de la phase de groupes du Championnat des nations, avec l’objectif de se qualifier pour la finale, prévue le 29 novembre, à Twickenham, au Royaume-Uni.

lemonde.title: Carlo Ossola, philologue : « Nous sommes des petits hommes sur les épaules de nos devanciers »
lemonde.description: Le professeur émérite de littérature italienne au Collège de France se revendique du modeste copiste. Cet humaniste, plutôt, éclaire le présent en dialoguant avec les auteurs du passé, comme en témoignent deux nouveaux livres, « Alléger le temps » et « L’Avenir de nos origines ».

lemonde.title: Le remorquage du cargo « Miro-G », échoué au large des Landes, pourrait durer plusieurs jours
lemonde.description: Selon la préfecture maritime, le déséchouement « nécessite la réunion de nombreux prérequis techniques », qui ne permettent pas de « garantir à ce stade le succès de cette opération ».

lemonde.title: Le boom des embauches dans le secteur médico-social cache les fragilités de l’économie sociale et solidaire
lemonde.description: Sans les créations d’emplois nécessaires pour accompagner le vieillissement de la population et le soin aux personnes âgées, l’ESS aurait perdu des postes sur un an.

lemonde.title: Au Sénégal, l’avenir incertain des installations des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse
lemonde.description: La piscine olympique et le stade Iba-Mar-Diop ont été rénovés pour la compétition, qui s’est tenue à Dakar du 31 octobre au 13 novembre. Désormais, plusieurs acteurs espèrent en récupérer la gestion.

lemonde.title: Inondations dans le Pas-de-Calais : deux cours d’eau en vigilance orange ; près de 800 évacuations depuis jeudi, selon la préfecture
lemonde.description: En Normandie, Vigicrues a prévenu que le niveau maximum de la Vire, placée en vigilance jaune, « est en passe d’être atteint ce [samedi] matin » dans le secteur de Saint-Lô et qu’il est « susceptible de générer des débordements localisés ».

france24fr.title: Verdict au procès de Michel Zecler : l'espoir d'une "jurisprudence"
france24fr.description: Dans votre magazine : les réactions après le verdict rendu hier soir en France dans le procès du passage à tabac de Michel Zecler. De la prison ferme pour les trois policiers reconnus coupables de violences aggravées, et de faux en ​écriture ‌publique. La circonstance aggravante de racisme a été retenue. Maitre Seydi Ba était notre invité.

france24fr.title: Manifestations en France : colère contre la vie chère et les violences policières
france24fr.description: Notre journaliste Sylvain Roussain est place de la République, au point de départ du cortège parisien. "Le renseignement annonce entre 15 000 et 30 000 manifestants", "ce qui n'empêche pas un dispositif policier important", rapporte-t-il. Ce sixième samedi de manifestations se tient juste après l'instauration d'une présomption d'usage légal des armes par les forces de l'ordre ce vendredi 20 novembre.

france24fr.title: Trump - Poutine : comment expliquer leur relation actuelle ?
france24fr.description: Donald Trump et Vladimir Poutine se sont rapprochés récemment, ce qui rend la position américaine assez illisible en ce qui concerne la guerre en Ukraine. Nous décryptons la situation avec notre invité Ronald Hatto, professeur de relations internationales à Sciences Po.

france24fr.title: Une "attaque de drone" contre un cargo russe détectée dans le golfe de Finlande
france24fr.description: Une "attaque de drone" contre un cargo russe dans le golfe de Finlande a été détectée par l'armée finlandaise, samedi, selon le ministère de la Défense du pays nordique, qui en a informé ses alliés au sein de l'Otan.

france24fr.title: Manifestations en France : la révolution en fanfare ?
france24fr.description: Au départ des récentes manifestations, il y a souvent un orchestre. La fanfare se poursuit ensuite dans le cortège : une façon d'exprimer sa colère autrement. "On peut danser une colère", assure une manifestante.

france24fr.title: Acte VI de la mobilisation : les manifestants se rassemblent place de la République
france24fr.description: Ce samedi 21 novembre, les manifestations reprennent à travers la France. Notre envoyé spécial Sylvain Rousseau est en direct de la place de la République, point de départ du cortège. "Il y a un appel à manifester dans différents pays d'Europe", rappelle-t-il.

france24fr.title: Manifestations à travers l'Europe contre la guerre et pour la jeunesse
france24fr.description: De Milan à Londres en passant par Amsterdam et Lausanne, des dizaines de milliers de manifestants se sont mobilisés vendredi à travers l'Europe contre la "militarisation" de la société et pour l'avenir des jeunes dans un climat de colère sociale alimentée par le coût de la vie.

france24fr.title: Lutte contre les gangs en Haïti : la coopération avec le Salvador s'intensifie
france24fr.description: Une nouvelle étape s'ouvre dans la coopération entre Haïti et le Salvador dans la lutte contre les gangs : la construction annoncée de plusieurs prisons.

france24fr.title: Le Danemark accuse la Russie d'avoir tenté d'assassiner un rappeur ukrainien
france24fr.description: Grand appui de l'Ukraine, le Danemark a accusé Moscou d'avoir fomenté une tentative d'assassinat d'un rappeur ukrainien sur son sol et va expulser l'attaché de défense de l'ambassade de Russie.

france24fr.title: Yémen - Arabie saoudite : nouvel échange de frappes entre les deux pays
france24fr.description: Les forces saoudiennes ont indiqué samedi 21 novembre avoir abattu trois missiles balistiques tirés par les Houthis yéménites pro-iraniens en direction de Riyad, au lendemain de frappes menées par l'Arabie saoudite au Yémen contre un port stratégique de la mer Rouge.

france24fr.title: Comprendre la relation franco-allemande, avec Hélène Miard-Delacroix
france24fr.description: Comment expliquer la montée en puissance de l'AfD en Allemagne ? Le tandem franco-allemand est-il toujours aussi solide ? Comment expliquer que de moins en moins de jeunes français choisissent d'étudier l'allemand, et inversement ? La réponse à toutes ces questions avec l'invitée du jour du podcast "Avec Judith", Hélène Miard-Delacroix, germaniste et historienne française.

france24fr.title: Ligue des nations : L'équipe de France retrouve l'Espagne en quarts
france24fr.description: Voilà une occasion de prendre leur revanche. Battus par l'Espagne en demi-finale de la Coupe du monde, en juillet dernier, les Bleus retrouveront la Roja en quarts de finale de la Ligue des nations, en mars prochain.

france24fr.title: Police : la présomption d'usage légal des armes entérinée au Parlement
france24fr.description: L'instauration d'une présomption d'usage légal des armes par les forces de l'ordre, mesure vivement combattue dans la rue par ses opposants qui l'assimilent à un "permis de tuer", a été définitivement adoptée au Parlement vendredi soir, à la veille d'une nouvelle journée de mobilisation sociale.

france24fr.title: France : acte VI de la mobilisation contre la vie chère
france24fr.description: Les manifestations reprennent ce samedi 21 novembre en France. C'est le sixième acte d'une mobilisation contre la vie chère. À Paris, le cortège partira de la place de la République.

france24fr.title: IA : un traducteur pour comprendre les animaux dans les années à venir ?
france24fr.description: L'IA pourrait permettre de saisire le language des animaux. Des scientifiques ont commencé a identifier un vocabulaire chez les élephants après avoir analysé plus de 900 enregistrements.

france24fr.title: L'IA déraille à Wall Street, le marché enregistre des centaines de milliards de dollars de pertes
france24fr.description: Wall Street a lourdement chuté vendredi 20 novembre, croulant sous le poids des inquiétudes persistantes autour de l'intelligence artificielle (IA), un jour à peine après la cotation historique du géant du secteur, Anthropic.

france24fr.title: Au procès Zecler, le racisme retenu, prison ferme pour trois policiers
france24fr.description: La cour criminelle de Paris a retenu ce vendredi 20 novembre la dimension raciste de l'agression de Michel Zecler en 2020 et condamné trois policiers à des peines allant de un an sous bracelet électronique à deux ans ferme, un verdict salué par les avocats du producteur de musique noir.

france24fr.title: En Pologne, la coalition pour l'Ukraine s'exerce à l'ombre de la guerre
france24fr.description: Réunie pour la première fois sur le terrain, une coalition pilotée par Paris et Londres a vocation à se déployer rapidement dès la signature d'un cessez-le-feu, pour aider l'Ukraine à dissuader à l'avenir toute nouvelle agression russe.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Neue Angriffe auf Tanker in umkämpfter Strasse von Hormuz
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Ein russischer Frachter wird im Finnischen Meerbusen von mutmasslich ukrainischen Drohnen getroffen
nzz.description: Das getroffene Schiff untersteht dem russischen Verteidigungsministerium. Ob es auch diesmal Waffen an Bord hatte, ist noch unklar. Während die Rettungsoperation läuft, verletzt ein russischer Militärhelikopter den finnischen Luftraum.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN WIRTSCHAFT - EU und Indonesien unterzeichnen weitreichenden Handelsdeal
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus der Wirtschaft.

nzz.title: Dramatische Wende 34 Jahre nach dem Mord am Mafia-Jäger Paolo Borsellino
nzz.description: Gianni De Gennaro, der frühere Polizeichef Italiens, hat sich das Leben genommen. Gegen ihn lief eine Untersuchung wegen Irreführung von Ermittlungen im Kampf gegen die Cosa Nostra.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die SVP macht Powerplay nach Drehbuch – sie weiss, sie kann sich das leisten
nzz.description: Mit Thomas Aeschi und Michael Graber nominiert die SVP zwei Hardliner für den Bundesrat. Ein ähnliches Manöver ist ihr schon einmal gelungen: mit Christoph Blocher und Ueli Maurer.

nzz.title: Mutmasslicher Drogenboss in Mexiko gefasst
nzz.description: Er steht auf der FBI-Liste der zehn meistgesuchten Flüchtigen. Mexikos Militär hat ihn nun in einem Grosseinsatz festgenommen.

nzz.title: VIDEO - So verliefen Europas Jugendproteste
nzz.description: Am Freitag gehen in mehreren europäischen Ländern junge Menschen auf die Strasse, unter anderem gegen Sparpolitik und Aufrüstung. Die Proteste bleiben grösstenteils friedlich.

nzz.title: Prozess um Palisades-Feuer in LA: Mann schuldig gesprochen
nzz.description: Anderthalb Jahre nach den Flächenbränden in Los Angeles war im Juni ein Prozess um Brandstiftung geplatzt. Die Jury konnte sich nicht einigen. Dann wurde der Fall neu aufgerollt.

nzz.title: Trump will Tech-Konzerne mit Datenzentren im Ausland hoch besteuern – und bleibt beim Ukraine-Krieg vage
nzz.description: Nach seiner Asienreise zieht Donald Trump Bilanz. Konkrete Fortschritte bei der nuklearen Abrüstung und im Ukraine-Krieg bleiben aus. Dennoch hofft er auf einen baldigen Frieden. Mit der Androhung von Strafsteuern für Tech-Konzerne sorgt er für eine Überraschung.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Trägt die Nato Schuld am Ukraine-Krieg? Die Mär von Russlands Sicherheitsinteressen
nzz.description: Moskau stellt sich als Opfer dar und fordert, dass sich das westliche Bündnis darum aus Osteuropa zurückzieht. Ein Blick in die Geschichte entlarvt dies als Lügenkonstrukt. Dem Kreml geht es um etwas ganz anderes.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «In der Schweiz leiden wir an einem Gletscherfetisch»
nzz.description: Diesen Sommer sind die Grundwasserpegel in der Schweiz vielerorts auf Rekordtiefs gefallen. Aber der Wasserexperte Klaus Lanz sagt, die Trockenheit lenke vom eigentlichen Problem ab.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Schweizer Abstimmungen: Chat-GPT taugt nicht für die Meinungsbildung
nzz.description: Befragt man KI-Chatbots zu Abstimmungsvorlagen, würden sie idealerweise alle Optionen neutral darstellen. Beim meistgenutzten Dienst passiert das noch nicht zuverlässig. Wer KI-Dienste zur Meinungsbildung heranzieht, muss sich bewusst sein, dass sie eine eigene politische Linie haben.

nzz.title: Das Genozid-Urteil gegen Myanmar hat auch für Israel Bedeutung
nzz.description: Erstmals überhaupt macht das höchste Uno-Gericht einen Staat für einen Völkermord verantwortlich. Es macht zudem klar, dass selbst ein legitimer Kampf gegen Terroristen eine Vernichtungsabsicht nicht ausschliesst.

nzz.title: Kaum ein Zuwanderer will die Schweiz wieder verlassen – doch nicht alle finden gleich schnell eine Arbeitsstelle
nzz.description: 42 Prozent der Bevölkerung haben einen Migrationshintergrund. Neue Zahlen zeigen, wie gut die Integration in den Arbeitsmarkt funktioniert und wo es noch Hürden gibt.

nzz.title: China will seine strengen KI-Regeln zum globalen Standard machen
nzz.description: An ihrem Gipfeltreffen in Shenzhen haben Donald Trump und Xi Jinping beteuert, bei der Regulierung künstlicher Intelligenz zusammenarbeiten zu wollen. Doch Einzelheiten blieben die beiden Staatschefs schuldig. Das hat Gründe.

nzz.title: Pakt mit dem Widersacher Europas: Frankreichs Grüne suchen ein Bündnis mit Mélenchon
nzz.description: Kaum eine Partei in Frankreich gibt sich so europabegeistert wie die Grünen. Deren Chefin Marine Tondelier will trotzdem mit dem linksradikalen Souveränisten Mélenchon koalieren. Sie hofft auf Parlamentsmandate – und auf mögliche Ministerposten.

zeit.title: George Harrison: »Ich musste das tun – aus Liebe zu George«
zeit.description: Die Witwe von George Harrison gibt kaum Interviews. Hier spricht sie über ihre Zeit mit ihm, seine Zeit mit den anderen Beatles – und wie sie den Mord an ihm verhinderte.

zeit.title: FIFA-Präsidentenwahl 2027: Afrikanischer Fußballverband unterstützt Infantinos Kandidatur
zeit.description: Der afrikanische Fußballverband spricht sich für Gianni Infantino als Fifa-Präsident aus. Damit folgt er der Wahlempfehlung des südamerikanischen Kontinentalverbands.

zeit.title: Fußball-Bundesliga: Spielergewerkschaft warnt Bayern vor Druck auf Musiala
Landtagswahl 2027: Nicole Baer ist AfD-Spitzenkandidatin im Norden
Fußball-Bundesliga: Zwei Freunde, ein Sieger: Hütters Eintracht bezwingt die TSG
Fußball-Bundesliga: Dortmund übernimmt Tabellenführung vom FC Bayern
Fußball-Bundesliga: Gruda trifft auch bei RB: Leipzig stürzt Union in die Krise
Bundesliga: Mainz will Negativserie beenden - FCK oben dranbleiben
Neue Spitze des Sozialverbands: Abgeordnete Rauscher nun Vorsitzende des VdK in Bayern
Russische Flugkörper in Polen: Nato-Chef Mark Rutte will »jeden Zentimeter« Polens verteidigen
zeit.description: Der Nato-Generalsekretär ist nach Warschau gereist, nachdem mehrere russische Flugkörper in Polen abgestürzt waren. Rutte sprach von einem »gefährlichen Vorfall«.

zeit.title: John Ausonius: Der »Lasermann« und seine rechtsextremen Taten
zeit.description: Mit einem Gewehr und Laserzielgerät schießt im Schweden der 1990er-Jahre ein Mann auf Einwanderer. Der »Lasermann« versetzt ein ganzes Land in Angst und Schrecken.

zeit.title: Howard Lutnick: Kostet die Nvidia-Affäre Trumps Lieblingsminister das Amt?
zeit.description: US-Wirtschaftsminister Howard Lutnick ist das loyalste Mitglied in Trumps Kabinett. Doch die Verbindungen seiner Familie zu Nvidia könnten ihn nun zu Fall bringen

zeit.title: Altersvorsorgedepot: Staatliches Depot für Zusatzrente verzögert sich wohl bis Sommer 2027
zeit.description: In wenigen Wochen startet das geförderte Altersvorsorgedepot. Doch die vom Staat angebotene Basisvariante kommt laut Bundesfinanzministerium wohl erst deutlich später.

zeit.title: »Braver New World« von John Kampfner: Nur Mut!
zeit.description: Viele politische Akteure wirken erschöpft und blicken ängstlich auf die Umfragewerte. Ein neues Buch könnte ihnen (und uns) neue Hoffnung geben.

observador.title: Associação quer que Governo explique medidas para menopausa
observador.description: A associação pretende que o Governo explique que respostas neste sentido vai concretizar, com que financiamento e em que prazo.

observador.title: Bezzecchi vence sprint. Queda de Marquez adia título
observador.description: O italiano Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia) venceu a corrida sprint do Grande Prémio de Portugal de MotoGP. Queda do espanhol Marc Márquez (Ducati) adiou a decisão do título mundial.

observador.title: Presidência da COP31 pede ação com responsabilidade
observador.description: A conferência, a mais importante reunião mundial sobre o clima, reúne quase 200 países em Antália e devia ter terminado na sexta-feira, mas divergências entre as partes impedem um consenso.

observador.title: Bruno Nunes: "O PSD tem sido pouco de direita"
observador.description: Em entrevista à Rádio Observador, Bruno Nunes explica porque desistiu da candidatura ao Conselho de Jurisdição Nacional do Chega, admitindo divergências que devem ser discutidas internamente.

observador.title: UE e Indonésia assinam acordo comercial "ambicioso"
observador.description: Segundo Bruxelas, o acordo deverá permitir aumentar as exportações da UE para a maior economia do Sudeste Asiático em cerca de 40% nos próximos 15 anos.

observador.title: As notícias das 16h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: City empata com Fulham, o 4º jogo sem vencer na Liga inglesa
observador.description: O inevitável Haaland marcou aos 25 minutos, mas o golo foi anulado por falta do avançado norueguês sobre o guarda-redes Bernd Leno.

observador.title: Suspensa greve dos tripulantes de cabine da Azores Airlines
observador.description: A greve dos tripulantes de cabine da companhia aérea açoriana Azores Airlines, prevista para os dias 01, 02 e 03 de dezembro, foi suspensa.

observador.title: Nações Unidas quer regular "robôs assassinos"
observador.description: Os países reunidos em Genebra para uma conferência da ONU sobre os "robôs assassinos" chegaram a acordo, após cinco dias de discussões, para abrir caminho a uma possível regulamentação internacional.

observador.title: FBI investiga ataque informático contra base de dados
observador.description: O FBI investigou na sexta-feira uma aparente intrusão informática no seu Centro Nacional de Informação Criminal ocorrida nos últimos dias.

observador.title: Governo argentino aprova megaprojeto de exportação de gás
observador.description: Argentina deu apoio a um projeto de exportação de gás natural liquefeito que prevê investimentos de 45,57 mil milhões de euros até 2050, montante sem precedentes na história do país.

observador.title: Bruno Nunes: "Não concordo com algumas questões funcionai...
observador.description: O deputado do Chega ponderou avançar com uma candidatura ao Conselho de Jurisdição e recuou a pedido de André Ventura, embora assuma discordâncias sobre o modo de funcionamento interno.

observador.title: Manteigas em alerta para chuva intensa após manhã tranquila
observador.description: O autarca agradeceu o comportamento das pessoas, que "até o momento, estão a acatar perfeitamente as instruções que efetivamos com a declaração de situação de alerta municipal".

observador.title: UE. Portugal com corte de 400 milhões em proposta de Costa
observador.description: Vários países criticam proposta. Portugal sofre corte de 400 milhões de euros na proposta do presidente de Costa para orçamento comunitário até 2034, num contexto de reduções transversais para os 27.

observador.title: Bolieiro: dinheiro do PRR para habitação foi "bem empregue"
observador.description: Governante salientou que o executivo, com o apoio dos gestores de projeto e a coordenação da Estrutura de Missão para o PRR, fez o que "muitos anunciaram, durante muito tempo, que seria impossível".

observador.title: Costa diz que interesses portugueses estão traduzidos na UE
observador.description: António Costa vincou que "Portugal está bem representado" nas reuniões do Conselho Europeu, pelo primeiro-ministro, Luís Montenegro.

observador.title: Discussão final do Orçamento do Estado com horário ajustado
observador.description: A convenção do Chega determinou o ajustamento dos horários da discussão e votação final do Orçamento do Estado para 2027. Esta vai acontecer na terça-feira à tarde.

observador.title: Atlético elimina Casa Pia da Taça de Portugal
observador.description: O golo solitário do defesa do emblema da Tapadinha foi marcado aos 21 minutos do encontro, colocando o Atlético nos oitavos de final da Taça, juntamente com o FC Porto, campeão nacional.

spiegel.title: Bundesliga: FC Bayern verliert Tabellenführung, Dortmund und Leipzig profitieren
spiegel.description: Der FC Bayern hat Sorgen – und die Konkurrenz nutzt das konsequent aus. Dortmund profitiert von einem Torwartfehler, Freiburg spielt wie eine Spitzenmannschaft und Leipzig beeindruckt mit einer starken Offensive.

spiegel.title: »Costa Concordia«: Kapitän Francesco Schettino darf das Gefängnis verlassen
spiegel.description: Beim Untergang der »Costa Concordia« kamen 32 Menschen ums Leben. Der damalige Kapitän, Francesco Schettino, ist seit gut neun Jahren in Haft. Nun durfte er unter Auflagen nach Hause.

spiegel.title: Mexiko: Heftige Feuergefechte bei Festnahme von Kartell-Boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores
spiegel.description: Wenn nicht die Polizei, sondern ein Verteidigungsministerium die Verhaftung eines Drogenbosses bekannt gibt, ist klar: Hier geht es um eine ganz große Nummer. Beim Zugriff auf Fausto Isidro Meza Flores kam es zu kriegsähnlichen Szenen.

spiegel.title: Gérard Depardieu und Michel Houellebecq: Vorwurf der gemeinschaftliche Vergewaltigung, Justiz ermittelt
spiegel.description: Eine Schauspielerin wirft Gérard Depardieu und Michel Houellebecq vor, ihr gegenüber sexuell übergriffig geworden sein. Die Frau hat den Schauspieler und den Schriftsteller verklagt, ein Verfahren wurde eröffnet.

spiegel.title: Russland: Warum der Kreml Angst vor zu klugen Schülern hat - Kolumne
spiegel.description: Erst traf es Rektoren und Eliteschulen, jetzt den Nachwuchs selbst: Russland drängt Jugendliche nach der neunten Klasse aus der Schule – und damit oft zur Armee. Russland wird zum Staat, der seine Bürger dumm hält.

spiegel.title: Hubert-Aiwanger-Trauerfeier: Tanja Schweiger dankt für Solidarität
spiegel.description: Familie, Weggefährten und Bürger haben von Hubert Aiwanger Abschied genommen. Seine Lebensgefährtin Tanja Schweiger, selbst Politikerin der Freien Wähler, dankte für Solidarität.

spiegel.title: Björn Höcke: Wiederwahl als Thüringer AfD-Chef
spiegel.description: Björn Höcke bleibt Chef der Thüringer AfD und sich treu: In einer Rede attackierte der radikale Politiker den Verfassungsschutz und die Reform der Geheimdienste.

spiegel.title: Jamal Musiala: Die FC Bayern-Patriarchen senden mit ihrer Demontage ein schlimmes Signal – Kommentar
spiegel.description: Statt dem wieder genesenen Musiala den Rücken zu stärken, demontieren die Bayern-Patriarchen ihn öffentlich. Sie zeigen damit, dass »Mia san mia« dann doch nicht mehr ist als ein Marketingspruch.

spiegel.title: Franziska Brantner: Grünenchefin kritisiert »Söder-Geschenke« zulasten Jugend
spiegel.description: Grünenchefin Brantner hat sich an die Seite der protestierenden Jugendlichen gestellt. Der Regierungskoalition warf sie eine »grausame Politik« vor und forderte mehr Geld für Schulen.

spiegel.title: Rollenspiele im Test: »Daggerheart«, »Midgard«, »Draconis« und »Storyfold«
spiegel.description: Wer seine Zeit gern mit Abenteuern in magischen Welten verbringen möchte, muss nicht weit reisen. Auf dem Spieltisch warten Hexen, Drachen, Götter und ein dunkler Wald auf Spielerinnen und Spieler.

spiegel.title: Julian Luginger: Tod von 11-jähriger Tischtennis-Hoffnung sorgt für Trauer und Fassungslosigkeit
spiegel.description: Er war der bestplatzierte Europäer in seiner Altersklasse: Der Österreicher Julian Luginger galt als eines der größten Talente im Tischtennis. Nun ist er im Alter von elf Jahren an Knochenkrebs gestorben.

spiegel.title: Uno-Klimakonferenz in Antalya: Frust und verhärtete Fronten beim Verhandlungsfinale
spiegel.description: Auch 20 Stunden nach dem offiziellen Ende des diesjährigen Klimagipfels in der Türkei stocken die Verhandlungen über die Abschlusserklärung. Verhandler sind frustriert, Ländergruppen heillos zerstritten. Die EU drohte sogar mit einem Scheitern.

spiegel.title: Rafael Nadal: Tennisikone wird in Vorstand von Real Madrid gewählt
spiegel.description: Nach 22 Grand-Slam-Titeln geht Rafael Nadal zukünftig auf die Jagd nach Champions-League-Trophäen. Der langjährige Fan der Königlichen übernimmt bei Real Madrid einen Vorstandsposten.

spiegel.title: Nvidia und Anthropic: Das steckt hinter dem Börsenbeben
spiegel.description: An den Finanzmärkten geht die Angst um. Die Kurse vieler Techaktien stürzen ab. Der Chiphersteller Nvidia hat binnen weniger Wochen fast die Hälfte seines Börsenwerts verloren. Was ist da los? Was Sie jetzt wissen müssen.

spiegel.title: TV-Interview von Karl-Heinz Rummenigge: Der Angriff auf Jamal Musiala
spiegel.description: Karl-Heinz Rummenigge stellt den neurologisch erkrankten Jamal Musiala in einem denkwürdigen Interview zur Schau, seine Zukunft und sein Gehalt infrage. Über einen einmaligen Vorgang in der Clubgeschichte.

spiegel.title: Mundgeruch: Die Ursache für schlechten Atem wird oft jahrelang übersehen
spiegel.description: Millionen Menschen riechen unangenehm aus dem Mund, häufig ohne es selbst zu bemerken. In einer speziellen Sprechstunde der Universitätsmedizin Göttingen zeigt Zahnarzt Tim Hausdörfer, wie man den schlechten Atem loswird.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump demütigt Vance und Rubio öffentlich
spiegel.description: Bei einer Pressekonferenz im Weißen Haus holt der US-Präsident plötzlich seinen Stabschef ans Mikrofon. Und teilt danach gegen Vize Vance und Außenminister Rubio aus.

spiegel.title: Formel 1 in Las Vegas: Max Verstappen zeigt George Russell den Mittelfinger
spiegel.description: George Russell und Max Verstappen werden wohl keine Freunde mehr. Nach einem Duell im freien Training zückte der Red-Bull-Pilot den Mittelfinger in Richtung des Engländers. Es ist nicht der erste Zwischenfall zwischen den Fahrern.

letemps.title: Robert Pattinson en James Bond, le choix du talent
letemps.description:
CHRONIQUE. Robert Pattinson sera le septième James Bond de l’histoire de la franchise. Et le premier à avoir eu une vraie carrière avant de devenir 007

phys-org.title: Babies in ancient Greek colony started solid food at 3 months but nursed for nearly 4 years, chemical signatures suggest
phys-org.description: Over 2,500 years ago, Himera was a Greek colony inhabited by local Sicilians, Phoenicians and Greeks. Despite their diverse cultural backgrounds, they all shared one thing: they began weaning their babies early and continued for a long time.

phys-org.title: An ancient failed rift is reawakening inside one of Africa's oldest landmasses
phys-org.description: In April 2017, a magnitude 6.5 earthquake shook southern Africa from an unlikely place: the middle of the Kalahari Craton in eastern Botswana. Cratons are the ancient cores of continents, and this one is built from blocks of crust up to 3.7 billion years old. Geologists have long considered such regions too cold, too thick and too rigid to tear apart.

phys-org.title: Fermi's 14-year all-sky map bridges astronomy's elusive 'MeV gap'

We've always had trouble measuring them in the "megaelectronvolt" (MeV) energy range, which astronomers have taken to calling the "MeV gap." phys-org.title: From screens in class to smart glasses, Norway rethinks new technologies
phys-org.description: Three years ago, a schoolteacher in Norway was reprimanded for putting his pupils' iPads aside to return to pen and paper. Now, the whole country is rethinking its approach to new technologies.

phys-org.title: What makes rock deep beneath continents break away and sink?
phys-org.description: We usually picture mountain building as rock being pushed upward. But deep beneath some mountain belts and volcanic arcs, the opposite can happen: dense rock at the base of the crust can become unstable, break away and sink hundreds of kilometers into the mantle, dragging part of the rigid outer shell of the Earth (the lithosphere) with it. Seismic images suggest that this process, known as lithospheric dripping, has occurred beneath the central Andes and California's Sierra Nevada.

phys-org.title: Device that measures strawberry skin's strength will aid breeders
phys-org.description: Resilient strawberry varieties will be more easily identifiable thanks to a tool developed by University of Queensland engineering students. The prototype measures the strength of strawberry skin, a key breeding consideration for the Australian Strawberry Breeding Program at Queensland's Department of Primary Industries.

phys-org.title: Quantum software matches classical benchmark for a molecular interaction
phys-org.description: Predicting how molecules interact is central to drug discovery: it offers important information about how a new drug might work in the human body, the side effects it can cause and more. Computationally modeling these interactions can reduce the need for lengthy and expensive lab work, but some interactions still remain beyond the reach of classical computers.

phys-org.title: The call of the seamount: Two new armored tardigrades described in the Atlantic
phys-org.description: An international team led by researchers from Senckenberg am Meer in Wilhelmshaven has described two new species of marine tardigrades. The tiny marine organisms were discovered in the sediment of the Senghor Seamount off the coast of Cape Verde. According to the researchers, the discovery underscores the role of undersea mountains as oases of biodiversity. The study, which includes comprehensive taxonomic descriptions of the new species, has been published in the journal "ZooKeys."

phys-org.title: Broadening the role of RNA: A messenger, a mediator and now a condensate coordinator
phys-org.description: New research about condensates—cellular compartments that act as hubs for facilitating biological reactions—continues to reveal novel insights into how cells function. phys-org.title: 'Forever' chemicals? Don't be so sure, says engineer
phys-org.description: Inside the disinfection room of Baltimore's Ashburton water filtration plant, 14 University of Maryland students clad in hard hats peered up at six towering vats of bleach used to treat water that flows from the distant Liberty Reservoir into the facility, killing bacteria and other pathogens before it's routed to the region's kitchen sinks.

phys-org.title: A fish as old as Montana—the blue sucker discovered to live well over 100 years
phys-org.description: Using bomb radiocarbon dating on microscopic otoliths (earstones), researchers have found that a native species of fish in the Upper Missouri River in Montana is living up to 130 years—more than triple the previous estimate of around 40 years—and some blue suckers alive today hatched in the late 1800s, around the dawn of the automobile and when Montana officially became a state.

phys-org.title: Caribbean corals are in crisis. Fossil reefs can help point to where corals may persist
phys-org.description: The fossilized remains of ancient coral reefs often sit just meters from living corals in the Caribbean, where reefs have declined sharply over the past 70 years. Those fossils could help show where corals might survive a warming future. In two new papers, researchers at The University of Texas at Austin identify which coral species dominated ancient reefs in northeastern Jamaica and suggest how that record could guide reef rehabilitation.

phys-org.title: Ancient bison hunting site in Texas challenges long-held assumptions
phys-org.description: For decades, archaeologists questioned whether Native American communities in the Southern Plains hunted bison by driving herds over cliffs, a sophisticated technique widely documented farther north.

phys-org.title: Scientists discover twist-tunable interlayer excitons in atomically thin anisotropic semiconductors
phys-org.description: When light shines on a semiconductor, negatively charged electrons and positively charged holes—empty states left behind when electrons move away—pair up and bind together. This bound state is called an exciton. When two atomically thin semiconductor layers are stacked, electrons and holes can reside in different layers, forming what is known as an interlayer exciton (IE).

phys-org.title: Gamified mobile payment features may drive adoption among Gen-Z users
phys-org.description: Gamified features in mobile payment applications may significantly increase adoption among consumers in emerging economies, with men and women responding in almost identical ways, according to research published in the International Journal of Business Information Systems.

phys-org.title: Record-setting X-ray laser reliably generates flashes with wavelengths shorter than distances between atoms
phys-org.description: Researchers from DESY and European XFEL have demonstrated reliable production and transport of X-ray laser flashes with a wavelength of about 0.04 nanometers (or a photon energy of 30,000 electronvolts) at European XFEL, raising their own world record. This means that the X-ray's wavelength is much shorter than typical distances between neighboring atoms in solids, which enables the study of materials with higher spatial resolution than before.

phys-org.title: Digital imaging workshop aims to reveal secrets in medieval manuscripts
phys-org.description: Researchers recently used multispectral imaging technology to try to uncover hidden information from medieval manuscripts at the Rare Book and Manuscript Library at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. The library hosted a digital imaging workshop in early October that served as a pilot study for how the technology can help analyze fragile, centuries-old documents.

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

proj-syn.title: Journalism Can Be More Than AI Fodder
proj-syn.description: As AI fundamentally alters the information environment, news publishers risk becoming little more than content suppliers for Big Tech. To avoid that fate, many are drawing on their archives and expertise to develop AI tools that allow them to operate and compete on their own terms.

proj-syn.title: Governing African Economies as They Are
proj-syn.description: Africa cannot overcome its development challenges by applying the same knowledge, economic, and innovation systems that helped create them. Imagining and governing new ways forward will require three intellectual ruptures.

proj-syn.title: Making Earth Cool Again
proj-syn.description: Climate multilateralism is evolving into a two-tiered system in which high-level negotiations toward shared commitments and the real-world implementation of climate solutions become more mutually supportive. Only by unleashing such virtuous cycles can we keep the 1.5ºC target for global warming within reach.

proj-syn.title: America’s Lame-Duck Autocrat
proj-syn.description: When autocrats suffer a defeat, they tend to double down, such as by intensifying repression at home or behaving more recklessly abroad. With two years left in office after historic midterm election losses, this is the road US President Donald Trump appears to be taking.

proj-syn.title: Getting Ukraine’s House in Order
proj-syn.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly opposed the idea of forming a national unity government. But bringing opposition leaders into the cabinet would ensure the checks on corruption and wayward bureaucratic action that Zelensky’s team can no longer provide.

proj-syn.title: What Adam Smith Missed
proj-syn.description: For all that he got right, the "founding father" of economics failed to see how technological innovations lead to market monopolization. If AI is left to the invisible hand, it will almost certainly increase economic and political inequality, causing even deeper social polarization and further undermining democracy.

proj-syn.title: China Ratchets Up Its Weaponization of Trade
proj-syn.description: Just as the US has been leveraging its large market and technological leadership for geopolitical ends, China is now using its dominance in critical minerals, industrial inputs, and specialized manufacturing machinery to coerce and punish other countries. The consequences, both economic and geopolitical, are far-reaching.

proj-syn.title: There Is Only One Thing to Talk About With Russia
proj-syn.description: The European security order’s foundational principle is never to tolerate aggression. There is no need to revise that order, as the Kremlin has proposed, only to wait for a Russian regime that is willing to respect other countries’ territorial integrity and uphold its own previous commitments.

proj-syn.title: The Truth About Global AI Governance
proj-syn.description: Because the current approach to global AI governance presumes that developing countries are full of eager adopters of AI who need to be cautioned about the technology's risks, it overlooks what their information environments and media markets actually need. A survey of researchers who study 71 countries sets the record straight.

proj-syn.title: Demography is the Achilles’ Heel of Dictatorships
proj-syn.description: Governments that manipulate population figures often end up deceiving themselves as much as the public. When autocratic leaders mistake inflated numbers for real national strength, they make costly strategic mistakes and fail to address their countries’ demographic decline until it is too late.

proj-syn.title: The Silver Lining of a Data-Center Slowdown
proj-syn.description: With leading AI labs under intense competitive pressure to keep advancing the frontier of the technology's capabilities, resistance to the build-out of computing resources is not such a bad thing. The more time we can buy, the greater our chances of maximizing the potential benefits and mitigating the risks.

proj-syn.title: What Nvidia’s Crisis Reveals About the Chip War
proj-syn.description: Export restrictions, like those depriving China of Nvidia’s most advanced chips, may buy time by curtailing a competitor's access to frontier capabilities made elsewhere. But in any technological conflict, policymakers must remember that slowing a rival is not the same as strengthening oneself.

proj-syn.title: When Export Restraints Are the Lesser Evil
proj-syn.description: Governments face pressure to protect domestic industries while preserving access to cheaper foreign goods. The recent EU-China car-export deal offers an uneasy compromise that protects European automakers while keeping Chinese cars available to consumers, making it preferable to prohibitive tariffs.

proj-syn.title: The Trade Losses That Nobody Counts
proj-syn.description: While much of the United Kingdom’s post-Brexit debate has focused on the monetary value of lost trade with the European Union, the composition of UK-EU trade flows warrants closer attention. A sharp decline in the variety of products shipped to Europe suggests that the economic costs have been greater than many realize.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Big Bet on Health Care
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s dependence on imported medicines and medical equipment leaves families exposed to exchange-rate fluctuations and hospitals at the mercy of global supply chains. Expanding domestic manufacturing is essential to reducing the cost of treatment and ensuring that more Nigerians can access quality care.

proj-syn.title: What Should the Nvidia Board Do?
proj-syn.description: The proper role of any corporate board is to strike a careful balance between stakeholders. In Nvidia's case, the board will have to consider not just the current trading price, but also how its decisions will affect the landscape in which it operates, its employees, and its license to trade.

proj-syn.title: The Roots of Macron’s Failure
proj-syn.description: Although French President Emmanuel Macron has certainly made mistakes, his troubled presidency is symptomatic of a deeper problem. In the end, he failed to build something truly enduring because he was seduced by the same monarchical impulse that is a recurring feature of French political culture.

proj-syn.title: Yalta in Shenzhen?
proj-syn.description: In principle, the planned summit of the US, Russian, and Chinese presidents could usefully address what should be done to limit the proliferation of nuclear weapons, ensure that AI is more a force for good than harm, and end ongoing wars and prevent new ones. But principle is one thing; in practice, we are likely to see something else.

crunchbase.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: Reflecting Sunlight From Space, Better Breathing And Smarter Garbage Trucks
crunchbase.description: What if solar farms could keep generating electricity after sunset with a little help from mirrors orbiting Earth? Or researchers could send an experiment into space for less than the price of a car? Our latest roundup also includes a company bringing AI to the old-school business of garbage hauling, another rethinking how factories are programmed, and a consumer brand betting that better breathing could become a big business.

crunchbase.title: What The Telecom Bust Taught Me About AI’s Debt Boom
crunchbase.description: The AI buildout’s growing reliance on debt echoes the telecom bubble, raising the risk that infrastructure spending will outpace the revenue needed to meet fixed repayment obligations. According to guest author David Spreng of Runway Growth Capital, even if AI fulfills its technological promise, borrowers’ survival will depend on realistic demand forecasts and debt tied to dependable cash flows, with missed timelines potentially forcing restructurings and bankruptcies.

crunchbase.title: The Blue Economy: The World’s Quietest Economic Engine And Its Smartest Cities
crunchbase.description: The $2.6 trillion blue economy is creating startup opportunities in maritime automation, clean energy and logistics, with blue tech funding nearing $10 billion through Q3 2026, driven largely by major defense deals. Alberto Onetti, chairman of Mind the Bridge, writes that ports are emerging as hubs for testing and scaling these technologies, but realizing their potential requires coordination among port authorities, startups, investors and policymakers.

crunchbase.title: What’s Next For Recruiting, Job Hunting And HR? More AI, Of Course
crunchbase.description: So far this year, venture backers have poured close to $4 billion into an assortment of global companies focused on recruiting, finding jobs and streamlining processes associated with HR and payroll management, Crunchbase data shows. Not surprisingly, the vast majority are also incorporating a heavy dose of AI.

crunchbase.title: Public Markets Are Frequently Wrong. The SaaSpocalypse Shows Us Why
crunchbase.description: The “SaaSpocalypse” selloff and uneven recovery exposed public markets’ difficulty distinguishing software companies that benefit from AI from those it threatens, particularly as deeply embedded platforms retain competitive advantages. In this guest essay, Richard Anton, co-founder and general partner of Oxx, argues that this volatility distorts private transaction pricing, undermines confidence in public ownership and makes IPOs less appealing to founders.

crunchbase.title: Anthropic Closes Up 17% After Massive IPO
crunchbase.description: The offering promises to be the public market event of the season, with the Claude creator seeing investor demand for shares well in excess of its capital-raising goals.

crunchbase.title: The Key Numbers I’m Watching As Anthropic Makes Its IPO Debut
crunchbase.description: Just three years after launching with zero revenue, Anthropic brought in $17 billion and says more than 11,900 customers now spend at least $100,000 a year. But its IPO filing also reveals enormous computing commitments and big questions about balancing growth with risks.

crunchbase.title: What To Measure When ARR Isn’t Enough
crunchbase.description: AI companies’ hybrid subscription, usage and outcome-based pricing makes headline ARR figures an unreliable measure of predictable revenue, often obscuring differences in customer commitments and spending patterns. Guest author Kenza Zayani, an early-stage investor at RTP Global, warns that as these businesses seek growth capital, investors increasingly expect evidence of retention, expansion, revenue predictability and sustainable margins to assess the durability of growth.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Investors Turn Up The Volume On Voice AI
crunchbase.description: Voice AI is drawing billions of dollars from investors as startups find more ways to put it to work. According to Crunchbase data, companies developing or offering the technology have raised at least $9.5 billion in venture funding so far in 2026.
